title: The Most-Searched Gen Alpha Slang of 2026
paragraphs: If you're over 30, you've probably found yourself Googling some of the words teenagers are using today.
And you're far from alone — in fact, millions of people have been searching for the meanings of these words every month!
Take "6-7," for example. Looking at Google search data from January 1 to August 27, word game website Unscramblerer found that there were around 1.6 million searches for this term each month.

The phrase comes from rapper Skrilla's song "Doot Doot (6 7)," and quickly went viral on social media — though it doesn't really mean anything! It became so popular that Dictionary.com named "6-7" its 2025 Word of the Year.
"6-7" also came first on Unscramblerer's list of the most-searched slang terms used by Generation Alpha — usually defined as people born after 2010.
Second on the list was "chud," a negative word for someone unpleasant or annoying. Third was "rizz," short for "charisma," used to describe someone's ability to attract people they like.
Another much-searched term was "mogging." To "mog" someone means to be better than them, especially in looks, clothes or fitness.

Then there's "larping." It comes from live-action role-playing games — or LARP — where people dress up and play fantasy characters in real life. "Larping" is now used to describe someone pretending to be something they're not — perhaps by trying to look rich or successful on social media.
Other popular searches included "cap," meaning a lie, and "no cap," meaning "for real" or "I'm not lying."
There was also "crash out," used for becoming very angry or losing control, and "sigma," often used online for someone seen as confident and cool.
And those are only a few. So if teenage slang sometimes sounds like another language, you're clearly not the only one trying to understand it!
